text: Facilities are old and not in great condition. But the staff are doing their best to provide competent care with limited resources. Wait times are unpredictable, for non-life threatening problems. Treatment for basic wounds and common ailments is fine and costs are very affordable. Recommended for basic services on a budget.

Myanmar government hospitals were bad, but this hospital is same too.  During my time living in Thailand, I have been to four government hospitals and three public hospitals, and this one is the worst. At least some of the nurses here are nice."

Have read a lot similar to my experience! I think the head nurse or heads in this hospital might be good but the subordinates aren't helping to keep the good image of the hospital due to reason known to them. The way they ignore you as a foreigner is inhumane and doesn't suit someone working in a public space. That's how I felt and I might be wrong tho but it wasn't a good experience. It appears private hospitals are suitable for foreigners. Understaffed and in bad condition. After three hours of waiting, I went to another hospital, was done in 30 minutes including prescription and pick up of medicine.

It was a good experience. The cost is very affordable even for a foreigner. The ER was a bit rushy but the nurse and the doctor were very kind and caring. They feed 4 meals a day and even changed into chicken for me for breakfast because I don’t eat pork.

Compare to other public hospital, Hang Dong Hospital is not a big and modern hospital. Everything is slow. There are queue after queue. But when thinking of professionalism, the medical staff and their teams work hard to help everyone. The service might not be good and quick when compare to other private hospital. It might not has a good parking area. There is no food around the hospital. But the service they gave to the patient, from my experience, it is decent.

So, if you're a tourist in the Hang Dong /  Chiangmai area DO NOT go to a private clinic or hospital ...Hang Dong hospital is a Government hospital with excellent medical professionals and good facilities ...inexpensive , thorough and invasive surgery is performed very well with great following care ...cost efficient and excellent care all in one ...

Guys, those who give 1-2 stars to this hospital. You write about poor parking and food, why? This is a hospital, not a supermarket. And yes, there may be a queue and have to wait. But is this the main thing? The professionalism of the doctors is what characterizes the hospital, not the parking lot. Sober up, please!

The hospital has bad employees and I really hate how their treat the patient and with their trash mouth. If you don’t like your job (they keep complaining about their job and put the anger to customer) and treat patient badly. Great people here . Been many times for different issues . Dog bite, blood work etc. Not all of the nurses speak english but you wont have any problems you ll be taken care of . Had a one night stay a few weeks ago . I felt the care was top notch . My room was clean comfortable and nursing staff excellent .

Awful experience. The covid registration area is a tent in the car park with far too many people packed in, babies, old people, obviously sick people, all unable to properly distance. Seats crammed together and no social distancing measures whatsoever. Gangways too narrow, people squeezing past each other and all made to share the same equipment, which wasn't being disinfected by anyone. And the equipment we used for blood pressure and oxygen didn't work properly anyway.
Plastic sheeting made it very poorly ventilated and incredibly hot, bad for everyone, especially people already feverish.
The most covid dangerous place I've experienced in Thailand and it's a government hospital. Really needs to be investigated.

Nurses aren’t the nicest people around. Facilities are adequate to treat most issues.

Very fast service even though covid times

The service was terrible, and the staff were quite unpleasant. The emergency room was incredibly slow. There are signs indicating the patient types and colors, and the waiting times are stated, but when I took my mother, she was classified as green, meaning she expected a 2-hour wait (if I remember correctly). However, we waited for 3 hours. We initially went around noon, unsure if it was dengue fever, as my mother had a high fever and was in pain. We went to room number 10, where they said the doctor wasn't there (only in the mornings). So, we took my mother to an outside clinic, costing 400 baht. When we presented the clinic's result – confirming dengue fever – we returned to room number 10, only to be made to wait outside the emergency room for another 3 hours. Then, they told us to go to room number 13 for a blood test. I don't understand why we needed another blood test when we already had a certificate from the clinic. And they said the doctor wasn't there (only in the mornings), but it was almost 6 PM when we went for the blood test, and the doctor was still there. It was very confusing. Why make us waste time going to the clinic and then coming back again? And the staff were very rude. The emergency room staff... I noticed that the elderly man was alone and had no relatives, so he seemed unaware of the situation. Instead of speaking in a polite tone, they spoke rudely to him, yelling. I felt sorry for him. I hope the hospital owner reads this and can improve the service, especially the speed of service.

I encountered an older nurse, seemingly experienced, but she seemed to be in a bad mood or just lazy for some reason. It felt like she was taking her anger out on my wound. She yanked off the tape with a loud "whoosh," making me inwardly curse. Usually, nurses remove bandages gently because it hurts. She cleaned my wound very carelessly and quickly, even though there weren't many people waiting for treatment. When I got home, I found she had taped over the wound again. I came to the hospital for a wound cleaning, but felt like my wound was abused. I went all the way to the hospital expecting this, and gas is scarce these days too. P.S. Not all nurses are like this, though.

When we first went in, we thought the nurses spoke loudly and were a little startled. But after going several times and opening our minds, we realized they just tend to speak loudly. We encountered many of them, but we saw that they also have their good points of speaking. We used the antenatal care and delivery rooms, and we completely overlooked the loudness. They provided excellent care and were very attentive to patients. Even though we were only using our government health insurance, we thought it was great. Thank you to all the nurses and doctors. We and your family are very grateful. 🙏🙏

All the doctors and nurses were very attentive and caring. They followed up on my mother's needs and were always happy to answer any questions, even over the phone.
From my experience being admitted to the hospital, I felt that even though it was a government hospital,
the care and attention were excellent. I was very impressed.

The emergency room has a very long wait. My younger brother has a cut and several abrasions from a motorcycle accident. There aren't many patients. The nurse asked if the pain wasn't too severe, and said to wait. We've been waiting for almost two hours already.

Instead of letting me into the treatment room and treating the wound first, they made me go in, hand in some documents, and have my blood pressure checked. Even though it wasn't a big wound, it was bleeding non-stop, but they made me sit and wait until the wound dried and I still wasn't allowed in. So I decided not to do anything. It was terrible. I've been to hospitals often in my life, but this hospital is beyond terrible.

Dr. Hang Dong is the best in my heart. We diagnosed cancer at Hang Dong Hospital and had surgery at Hang Dong Hospital. I have to thank Dr. Chanathip and the medical team at Hang Dong Hospital from the bottom of my heart. Today, more than a …

text: I can't say whether I was impressed or disappointed. Many times when I've been there, the wait times are long due to the large number of patients, which I understand. However, some staff members, quite a few, speak impolitely. Their answers are unclear, they point in the wrong direction, and when I ask again, they get irritated. But on my most recent visit, I was very impressed with the nurse at desk 2 (the one in the green uniform) who took my medical history. She spoke clearly and explained things clearly. Even during lunchtime, when many others were on break, this nurse still came to desk 4 to process my referral form. I had waited a long time, but she tried her best to get it done, speaking in a respectful tone and explaining everything to me. I understood and felt much better after the long wait; I wasn't angry at all about the wait. I've encountered this nurse two or three times before, and each time she's been consistently kind. 🙏🙏 I sincerely commend her.

Very bad. The nurses are foul-mouthed and work very slowly. There was a car accident and a broken bone. It took 3 hours for the wound to be treated. I waited in front of the wound dressing room, but no one paid attention for the entire 3 hours. When I went for an X-ray, the bones kept hitting me from one angle to another. They even used my bed to hit the door to get into the X-ray room. When the cast was put on, the doctor didn't know how to put it on. He wrapped my finger so tightly that it was squeezed by the cast. My finger was crooked and hurt so much. I had to come to another hospital to have the cast removed. It's really bad. The hospital that removed the cast said that they definitely don't know how to put it on, so they put it on like this. Another thing that's suspicious about the hospital where I had the cast changed is that they didn't explain how to care for the cast and didn't explain anything to me. I wasn't the only one who experienced this. That's all I'll say. When I got in the rescue vehicle, the rescuers told me to go somewhere else because this place was slow. But I really couldn't take it anymore, so I chose this one. In the end, I waited for more than 3 hours, and it was the most torturous 3 hours for me at a hospital that shouldn't be a hospital.

The registration counter staff, a bald man, was incredibly rude. This happened on July 27th, 2023, around 2 PM.
I spoke politely and respectfully, but he responded with a very rude tone and language. I suggest he quit and find a new job; this job doesn't suit someone with his personality.
Don't worry, I always pay cash when I go to the hospital.
I usually patiently go to a nearby hospital, but I don't have time to go to the Hang Dong branch. After this experience, I prefer going to the nearby hospital instead.
If you need to get a certificate or anything similar, I recommend the nearby hospital.
I was in a car accident and received excellent service from the nearby hospital.

This is the worst hospital I've ever encountered. Even hospitals in the provinces aren't this bad. I had a referral from another hospital, just to have blood drawn because it's closer to home, but I'm still receiving treatment at my …

On September 23, 2025, two of my friends were in a car accident and waited outside the emergency room. One friend was seriously injured, while the other had minor injuries. The less injured friend was treated first and even treated rudely, while the seriously injured friend had to wait a long time. Even just a "slight" movement resulted in the doctor scolding them – I'm baffled how someone with such behavior could be a doctor. Furthermore, because the doctor was treating the seriously injured friend's wounds painfully, they cried, and just a slight cry resulted in the doctors in the room ganging up and scolding them, calling them "ugly." I'm so confused. Was they poorly raised or is it just their personality? And this wasn't the first time the doctors behaved like this. While waiting for my injured friend, I saw a doctor kick a patient out because they wouldn't lie down. That patient politely asked if they could sit, but the doctor just kicked them out and refused to treat them. It was a terrible experience. If I had other hospital options, I would never go to this one.

Today, I took my child to the emergency room because he was crying so hard he was vomiting up a lot of milk, and he seemed to have mucus in his throat and was crying nonstop. When I arrived at the emergency room, I told the nurse at the front desk that it was normal and to go to room 10 if I was uncomfortable. After I finished, an elderly nurse came in to take a medical history and ask about his condition, but her words were so rude that it's unacceptable to live this long.
She then went into the emergency room while my child was still crying nonstop and vomiting again. Then a nurse shouted, "My child has had this problem too. I'm 5 now and I'm fine," and she looked displeased at the child's crying. When I left the room, the nurse at the front desk said the doctor needed to come, but she didn't know when he would come, or if she wasn't comfortable, she could go to another hospital. **** I want to ask, if you were the child of one of those nurses, would you bring your own child here for treatment? Are the hospital personnel untrained? How did they graduate? If they knew what to do or knew what was wrong with your child, they wouldn't have come to the doctor. If they had come, they wouldn't have encountered such foul-mouthed people.

The nurses are talking really badly. What's going on? What kind of nurse is she? She doesn't understand what she's saying. She's talking rudely and is really unpleasant.
